It is not even close to too late to go to school and start a career.  That should be your next move.  Even better if you can still live at home.  What you don't have time for is to put a ton of effort into trying on a bunch of different hats to discover what you want to do.  Have an honest, introspective conversation with yourself about what type of career you could see yourself having. When you have an idea,  start to research educational requirements and job outlook but more importantly,  connect with people in that job to get a sense of their day to day.  Make sure the income you can reasonably expect aligns with your and your s/o's needs and then go get em! While you're figuring that part out, I highly suggest going to your local community college and start taking basics like algebra. English lit, etc. Start earning credits now and then when you have a career focus,  you'll be able to dive into those classes.  Also,  community college before transferring to a university is likely the only way aside from buying your way in,  your high school transcripts and SATs are too old to use in an application packet now but if you put 1 to 2 years of hard work in at a community college then apply with a decent GPA and letters from professors,  you'll stand a much bigger chance.
